deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: What are the four bolt moves?
back: Up (unlocks, cocks), back (extracts), forward (feeds), down (locks). UBFD.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: What does lifting the Tikka bolt handle do?
back: Turns the locking lugs out of the receiver and cocks the firing pin.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: Name the six links of the firing chain.
back: Trigger, sear, firing pin, primer, powder gas, bullet.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: What do the locking lugs do?
back: Turn into recesses in the receiver and hold the pressure of the shot.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
back: Its claw grips the case rim and pulls the fired case out of the chamber.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
back: Grooves are the cut spiral channels. Lands are the raised ridges between them.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
back: Across the bore, land to opposite land (hunter education).

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
back: One full turn of the rifling every 10 inches of barrel. Lower number, faster spin.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: Your Arctic barrel length and twist (Sako spec)?
back: 508 mm (20 inch), 1:10 twist. Check your barrel stamp.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: About how fast does a 150 gr .308 spin?
back: About 3,400 turns a second at 2,820 fps from a 1:10 twist.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: Tikka factory trigger weight and range?
back: About 3 lb (13 to 15 N). Adjustable 2.5 to 4 lb. Never below 2.5 lb.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: What does Sako list as the Arctic trigger type?
back: Two stage: take up, a wall, then the break.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: Tikka: what does safety ON lock?
back: The bolt closed, the firing pin cocked, and the sear and trigger.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
back: Safety OFF. Ready to fire.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: Which rifle opens its bolt with the safety on?
back: The CZ 457. The Tikka two position safety locks the bolt.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
back: Muzzle safe, finger off, safety off, magazine out, bolt out, look through chamber, bolt in, decock pointing safe.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
back: Keep it pointed safe, wait at least one minute, then unload with extreme care.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: Tikka action screw torque, metal guard?
back: 7 Nm (62 in lb). Plastic guard: max 5 Nm (44 in lb).

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
back: Trigger feels different, misfire, safety fails, gas spits or primer pierced, bulged or split case, odd sound.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: Arctic iron sights: factory zero and range?
back: Zeroed at 100 m. Rear drum steps 100 to 600 m.

deck: How a rifle works: your Tikka T3x
front: Is a removed magazine proof the rifle is unloaded?
back: No. A round can still be in the chamber. Look.

deck: How a cartridge works
back: Case, primer, powder, bullet. CPPB.

deck: How a cartridge works
front: Which three stamps must match before you load?
back: Barrel stamp, box label, headstamp on each round.

deck: How a cartridge works
back: An explosive compound that ignites the powder when struck by the firing pin.

deck: How a cartridge works
front: Smokeless powder in the open air does what?
back: Burns slowly. It builds pressure only when confined in a chamber.

deck: How a cartridge works
front: Why does the case swell when fired?
back: Pressure presses the brass to the chamber walls, sealing the gas so it only pushes forward.

deck: How a cartridge works
back: Centrefire: primer in the centre of the base, most reloadable. Rimfire: priming in the rim, not reloadable.

deck: How a cartridge works
front: Name the parts of a rifle case.
back: Rim, extractor groove, body, shoulder, neck. Headstamp on the base.

deck: How a cartridge works
front: Name the parts of a hunting bullet.
back: Tip, ogive (curved nose), shank, base (flat or boat tail).

deck: How a cartridge works
front: How many grains in a pound?
back: 7,000. So 150 gr is about 9.7 g.

deck: How a cartridge works
front: Cup and core bullet: strength and weakness?
back: Cheap, accurate, opens fast. Core can separate at high impact speed.

deck: How a cartridge works
back: Core fused to the jacket so they stay together for deep penetration.

deck: How a cartridge works
back: A copper wall splits a front core that opens and a rear core that keeps driving.

deck: How a cartridge works
front: Monolithic copper bullet: pro and con?
back: Keeps nearly all its weight, lead free. Needs speed to open; check the maker minimum.

deck: How a cartridge works
front: Can you hunt with full metal jacket in BC?
back: No. Full metal jacketed non expanding, tracer, incendiary and explosive bullets are unlawful for hunting with a rifle.

deck: How a cartridge works
back: The bullet mushrooms, making a wider wound channel for a quick kill.

deck: How a cartridge works
back: Do not fire ammunition over 10 years old.

deck: How a cartridge works
front: Name four faults to check on each round.
back: Split neck, dents, corrosion, loose bullet, wrong headstamp, too old.

deck: How a cartridge works
back: Primer, powder, wad, shot, crimp.

deck: How a cartridge works
front: Deer bullet choice for your .308 (ammo session)?
back: 150 gr cup and core or bonded. One load, zeroed.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
back: Internal (barrel), external (air), terminal (animal).

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
front: Why does the bullet cross the line of sight twice?
back: The scope sits above the bore, so the bore tilts up. The bullet climbs through the line, then falls back through it at the zero.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
front: Drop with a 100 m zero at 150, 200, 250, 300 m (150 gr)?

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
back: 1 MOA = 2.9 cm. 1 mil = 10 cm.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
front: 250 m hold on a 100 m zero in MOA?
back: About 3.8 MOA, about 15 clicks of 1/4 MOA, about 1.1 mil.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
front: Which clock directions are full value wind?
back: 3 and 9 o clock.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
front: Wind from 1 or 11 o clock counts as?
back: About half. 45 degrees: about 70%.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
back: About 27 cm. More than the vital zone.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
front: Double the distance, the wind drift?
back: About four times.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
back: Felt on the face, leaves rustle.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
front: Uphill or downhill: which distance for the hold?
back: The flat (horizontal) distance. Holding for the slope distance hits high.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
back: Slope distance × cosine of the angle. cos 30 = 0.87.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
front: Deer 250 m away, 30 degrees up. Hold for?
back: About 217 m. Holding for 250 hits about 10 cm high.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
back: About 1,700 J (1,250 ft lb).

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
back: About a quarter second (0.26 s).

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
front: Does altitude add or reduce drop?
back: Thin air reduces drop slightly: about 3 cm less at 300 m at 1,200 m elevation.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
front: Point blank range of a 100 m zero, 15 cm zone?
back: About 170 m of centre hold.

deck: Ballistics deep dive: drop, wind, angles, energy
front: What goes on your dope card?
back: Your load, zero, drops and holds at 150 to 300 m, wind at 20 km/h, and your max range. From your own groups.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
front: Guess 250 m, deer at 300 m. Result?
back: About 20 cm low with a 100 m zero: under the heart or a leg.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
front: How does a laser rangefinder measure?
back: It times a light pulse to the target and back.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
back: Roughly half. One maker lists 900 yd on deer for its 1800.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
back: Brace it, box on the body, three readings. Brace, box, three.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
back: The beam hit brush in front. Find a gap.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
back: Metres = size in metres × 1,000 ÷ mils.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
back: Yards = size in inches × 95.5 ÷ MOA.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
back: 230 m. The 46 cm deer size is hunter lore: a check only.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
front: Second focal plane reticle ranging rule?
back: Only at the power the manual names, usually the highest.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
back: Picture a known 100 m and count how many fit. Not accurate past 400 m.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
back: Compare how the animal looks with known distances: detail fades and the outline blurs with range.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
front: Name 3 things that make a deer look nearer.
back: Bright light with sun behind you, over snow or water, clear mountain air, strong contrast, a hidden dip.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
front: Name 3 things that make a deer look farther.
back: Poor light or fog, sun in your eyes, only part showing, blending in, lying down.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
back: Judge the distance to halfway, then double it.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
back: Decide near and far limits, add them and halve.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
front: How do you learn your pace count?
back: Walk a measured 100 m three times counting each left foot; average it.

deck: Judging distance: rangefinders, reticles and your eye
back: Guess out loud, then laser it, and log the error.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
front: Steadiest to least: four basic positions?
back: Prone, sitting, kneeling, standing.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
back: Bone. Stack the elbows under the rifle, then relax.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
back: Where the barrel points when your muscles are relaxed and you are supported.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
front: Crosshair drifts off when you relax. Fix?
back: Move your body around a pivot, not the rifle, until it settles on target.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
front: Barrel directly on a rock shoots?
back: High. Pad under the forend (hunter education).

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
front: Prone with a pack: where does the pack go?
back: Under the forend, not the barrel. Rear hand fine tunes height.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
front: How do you load a bipod?
back: Lean your shoulder gently forward, same pressure every shot.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
back: Crossed ankle (low, steady), open leg (slopes), with sticks (over grass).

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
back: Two legs toward you, one toward the deer, top about armpit height, feet nearly square.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
back: Sit facing downhill, heels dug in.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
back: Prone or kneel with the pack, or sit with sticks.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
back: Hand or glove between the rifle and the bark.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
front: Five steps from walking to steady?
back: Stop, say the position, sticks out and sit, rifle in and NPOA check, safety off when ready.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
front: When does the safety come off?
back: When the crosshair is settled and you are ready to fire.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
back: First shot of the day, from sticks or sitting, at hunting distance, on a 20 cm plate.

deck: Shooting positions and rests: drills that work in the field
back: 3 shots each prone, sitting, sticks at 100 m. All in 10 cm per position.

deck: A season practice plan: dry fire, range days, field shooting
front: Four parts of the shooting year?
back: Off season, build, tune, season.

back: Confirm zero at 100 m, 3 shots, cold barrel.

deck: A season practice plan: dry fire, range days, field shooting

back: Change load, scope or rings. Each change needs a new zero.

deck: A season practice plan: dry fire, range days, field shooting
back: Dry fire, range, field.

deck: A season practice plan: dry fire, range days, field shooting
back: All ammunition out of the room.

back: No. Good for loading practice, but they do not protect the firing pin (Tikka).

deck: A season practice plan: dry fire, range days, field shooting

back: Say "finished", snap cap out, rifle locked away before ammo returns.

deck: A season practice plan: dry fire, range days, field shooting
front: First shot of every range day?
back: A cold shot from a field position. Log it.

deck: A season practice plan: dry fire, range days, field shooting
back: Adjust only if the group centre is off by more than about 2.5 cm.

deck: A season practice plan: dry fire, range days, field shooting
back: About $2.05 to $2.75 versus $0.14 to $0.17 (price checked 2026-10-01).

deck: A season practice plan: dry fire, range days, field shooting

back: No recoil hides a flinch. Mix in .308 shots.

deck: A season practice plan: dry fire, range days, field shooting
front: Where can you shoot a field course?
back: A range, or land where discharge is lawful and safe with a backstop.

deck: A season practice plan: dry fire, range days, field shooting
front: Five things to log for each counting shot?
back: Date, position, distance, wind, result.

deck: A season practice plan: dry fire, range days, field shooting
back: A jerked trigger or flinch.

back: After any knock, fall, long rough drive or flight.

Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
front: Tikka: how soon can corrosion start?
back: Within 24 hours, even on stainless and all weather rifles.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
back: After every use, even with no shot fired (Tikka).

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
back: Unload; dry if wet; solvent brush; patches until clean; bolt, chamber, receiver; thin oil and screws.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
front: Which way does the rod go?
back: From the breech, through a bore guide, in the bullet direction.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
back: Locking lugs, cocking cam, head of the cocking piece. Lightly.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
back: Wipe the chamber dry and run a dry patch.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
back: At least once a year, more with heavy use or before storage.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
back: Can make the barrel shoot inaccurately and corrode more easily.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
back: Out of the case, dry it warm, then clean and oil.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
front: Why no leather or fabric case for storage?
back: They attract moisture even when they look dry (Tikka).

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
front: CZ advice in very low temperatures?
back: Remove oil from accessible parts or use a lube made for the cold.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport

back: Water beads form. Leave it cased somewhere cold and secure, or dry it well (Tip).

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
front: Muzzle in snow after a fall?
back: Unload, bolt out, look through. Obstruction: do not fire.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
back: Remove it, clean and oil the threads, refit snug.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
front: Loaded firearm in or on a vehicle in BC?
back: Not allowed. Chamber and attached magazine empty.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport

back: Locked trunk or lockable compartment; no trunk, out of sight and the vehicle locked.

deck: Cleaning, maintenance, cold and wet weather, transport
back: Locked away, ammunition in a separate locked place, dry.
